description: Compute a turn-by-turn route between origin and destination (optionally via waypoints). Costing "auto" = car, "truck" = lorry, "bicycle", "pedestrian" = walking, "motor_scooter" = moped. Pass `truck` {height_m, width_m, length_m, gross_weight_t, hazmat, tunnel_code} to apply dimensional limits and the ADR dangerous-goods tunnel matrix to the search; `pedestrian` {use_lit 0-1, type "wheelchair"|"blind", max_hiking_difficulty 1-6} for lit-street walking, accessibility and trail limits; `bicycle` {bicycle_type, use_roads 0-1, use_living_streets 0-1, avoid_bad_surfaces 0-1, use_hills 0-1} for quiet-ride and surface preferences. Returns distance (m), duration (s), maneuvers, polyline6 geometry and the ADR costing that was applied. Any of truck, auto, bicycle, pedestrian or motor_scooter routes may set `rationale: true` (opt-in, costs up to 1 + N extra routing calls) to learn which declared truck constraints or avoidance-side preferences (hills, surfaces, tolls, unlit streets, …) actually changed the route (`rationale.avoided[]`, basis route_divergence — it proves a field was binding, it does not identify the physical restriction or feature, and no live traffic or incident data is ever attributed). ADR honesty: `applied_adr.forbidden_tunnel_categories` describes the LOAD, not the returned route, and `applied_adr.tunnel_enforcement` states the boundary: roads are excluded only where the routing graph records an ADR tunnel category, so an unchanged route is not a clearance. Set `landmarks: true` for turn instructions anchored to recognisable places — each manoeuvre that passes one gains a `landmark_instruction` like "Turn right just after the Shell garage" beside the engine's own street-name `instruction`, which is never replaced. Prefer reading it aloud: it is how a passenger gives directions. Nothing is named unless it is recognisable from the road, within 40 m of the junction and not tagged as closed, so many routes return none and a `landmarks.annotated` of 0 with no `note` means this route genuinely passes nothing recognisable. Needs the MapMap gateway (GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY), whose place index does the lookup. Through the gateway each manoeuvre also carries the road it starts on: `country`, `subdivision`, `ref` (route numbers only), `road_class`, `speed_limit_unit` (`mph` or `km/h`, from the road's country), `speed_limit_sign` (`vienna` or `mutcd`), `speed_limit_posted` (the limit as the sign shows it, in the road's unit) and `driving_side`; each is absent when the map does not know it, never guessed. Optional `exclude_polygons` for what-if scenarios ("close this bridge and re-route"): an array of polygons, each an array of [lon, lat] pairs forming one ring — longitude FIRST — whose intersecting roads are excluded from the search. Applies to the Valhalla engine; unsupported on the GraphHopper engine, where it is ignored. Optional `avoid` and `exclude` name road features to keep off, and the difference between them is not cosmetic. `avoid` ("tolls", "highways", "ferries") is a PREFERENCE: it sets the costing's willingness to zero, and the engine's own reference says that is not guaranteed to avoid the feature — measured, avoiding tolls across the Dartford Crossing returns the same tolled route, because the untolled alternative is fifty kilometres further. `exclude` ("tolls", "highways", "ferries", "bridges", "tunnels") is a hard exclusion: it can answer NO ROUTE rather than a detour, and it depends on the routing engine's own hard-exclusion setting, which the engine does not report and this server cannot read — so it is requested, never promised. "tolls" and "highways" under `avoid` exist only on motorised costings; asking for one on a bicycle is refused rather than silently ignored. Whatever is applied comes back in `avoidance`, with the caveats — relay them, because "avoid tolls" read as a guarantee is the failure mode here. Each location also takes a kerbside approach: `preferred_side` "same" (alias "curb") stops on the door's side of the road, resolved against the locale's driving side — the left kerb in the UK, the right in Germany — with "opposite" and "either" (alias "unrestricted") for the rest. It is a snapping preference, not a manoeuvre guarantee, and it needs a coordinate genuinely offset from the road centreline; `street_side_tolerance_m` and `street_side_max_distance_m` bound the window in which it applies, and a pair leaving no window is refused rather than answered with the preference silently inert. Pass `emissions` {vehicle_category, fuel, euro_standard} for UK clean-air-zone assessment: the response's `zones` block then names every zone the route enters and what THIS vehicle pays there, with the publishing authority cited. Without it a zone can only be named, never priced. Needs the gateway, which holds the curated zone dataset; the whole dataset — every scheme, charge, boundary and provenance record — is readable at `GET /v1/zones` on the HTTP API when an agent needs to audit a figure or list zones without routing. Set `scenic: true` (auto costing only) to ask whether there is a prettier way. It is a PEER OFFER, never a substitution: the route in `geometry_polyline6` is byte-for-byte what the same request returns without the flag, and the prettier way, when there is one, arrives beside it in `scenic`, with its own geometry in `scenic.alternative_geometry_polyline6` and what it costs in `scenic.spoken` ("About seven minutes longer than the quick way"). EVERY OFFER STATES ITS REASON OR THERE IS NO OFFER: a route that scores well but cannot support a plain sentence is dropped rather than dressed up, so a `scenic.reason` of null means nothing here measured above the floor. That is an ANSWER, not a failure, and it is the one to relay. A REJECTION IS ALSO AN ANSWER: every candidate that lost says why in `scenic.rejections[]` (`same_route`, `no_scenic_gain`, `not_scenic_enough`, `over_time_budget` with the minutes it would have cost, `nothing_to_say`), so "no prettier way" is always attributable and raising the budget is an informed choice. It is a re-ranking of routes the engine already proposed, not a scenic search: a beautiful road the engine never offered was never considered, and `scenic.caveats` says so. Like `rationale`, IT COSTS EXTRA METERED COMPUTATIONS, at most two, which is why it is opt-in and never on by default. `available: false` with a `note` means this deployment could not look, which is not the same claim as nothing being there. Needs the gateway, whose basemap archive the scoring is measured against.

AvoidFeature.description: A road feature to avoid as a PREFERENCE, not a ban. "tolls" and "highways" apply to motorised costings only (auto, truck, bus, motor_scooter, motorcycle); "ferries" applies to every costing. Asking for one on a costing whose engine table has no field for it is refused rather than silently ignored.

BicycleSpec.description:
Bicycle options for costing "bicycle": the bicycle type plus road,
surface and hill preference weights, mapped onto Valhalla
`costing_options.bicycle`.

avoid_bad_surfaces.description:
Avoidance of surfaces unsuited to the bicycle type, 0.0–1.0
(1.0 = strictly avoid bad surfaces).

bicycle_type.description:
Bicycle type: "road", "hybrid" (default), "city", "cross" or
"mountain". Sets default speed and surface tolerance.

use_hills.description:
Willingness to take hills, 0.0–1.0 (0.0 = avoid climbs even at the
cost of longer routes).

use_roads.description:
Willingness to ride roads alongside motor traffic, 0.0–1.0
(0.0 = prefer cycleways and quiet streets — the quiet-ride slider).

CostingKind.description:
Costing models exposed by the MCP tools (a deliberate subset of the
Valhalla costing list), serialised in snake_case exactly as Valhalla
names them.

oneOf.description: Standard car costing.

Truck costing; honours dimensional limits and, when a `truck`
profile is supplied, ADR dangerous-goods restrictions.
Bicycle costing; tune it with a `bicycle` options object.

Pedestrian (walking) costing; tune it with a `pedestrian` options
object (lit streets, wheelchair/blind, hiking difficulty).

Motor scooter (moped) costing: like auto but prefers lower-speed
roads and may use ways closed to larger motor vehicles.

EmissionsFuel.description: What a vehicle burns, in clean-air-zone scheme terms.

oneOf.description:
Petrol, including petrol hybrids (schemes rate a hybrid by its
combustion engine's approval).
Diesel, including diesel hybrids.
Battery-electric.
Hydrogen fuel cell.
LPG or CNG; rated as petrol by every scheme in the dataset.

EmissionsSpec.description:
A vehicle's emission declaration, for clean-air / low-emission zone
assessment.

euro_standard.description:
Its Euro emission standard, 1–6. Heavy-duty approvals are written
in Roman numerals (Euro VI); declare Euro VI as `6`. Required for
any combustion fuel — without it no zone can be resolved, and a
half-declared vehicle is indistinguishable from an undeclared one.
Optional only for `electric` or `hydrogen`.

vehicle_category.description: What kind of vehicle this is, in scheme terms.

EmissionsVehicleCategory.description:
What a vehicle is, in clean-air-zone scheme terms.

Declaring this turns "charge depends on vehicle emissions" into an
answer. Without it a zone can only be named, never priced.

oneOf.description: A private car.
A van or light goods vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes.
A minibus (typically 8+ passenger seats, up to 5 tonnes).
A heavy goods vehicle over 3.5 tonnes.
A bus over 5 tonnes.
A coach over 5 tonnes.
A licensed hackney carriage.
A private hire vehicle.
A motorcycle, moped or tricycle.
A motor caravan or campervan.

ExcludeFeature.description: A road feature to exclude outright. A hard exclusion can leave a request with no path at all — that is the honest answer, not a failure — and it depends on the routing engine's own hard-exclusion setting, which nothing here can read.

PedestrianSpec.description:
Pedestrian options for costing "pedestrian": lit-street preference,
accessibility type and hiking difficulty, mapped onto Valhalla
`costing_options.pedestrian`. All preferences, never guarantees — the
router prefers matching ways where the map data supports it.

max_hiking_difficulty.description:
Maximum hiking-trail difficulty the route may use, as OSM
`sac_scale` 1–6 (1 = well-cleared, mostly flat trails; 6 =
demanding alpine terrain). Default 1.

type.description:
Pedestrian type: "wheelchair" (avoids steps, kerbs and steep
grades where mapped) or "blind" (richer guidance detail). Omit for
the default on-foot profile.

use_lit.description:
Preference for lit streets, 0.0–1.0 (1.0 = prefer lit paths as
strongly as possible — the "walk me home on lit streets" option).
Unlit ways are still used when no lit alternative exists.

PreferredSideKind.description:
Side-of-street preference for arriving at or departing from a location.

Carries both vocabularies: MapMap's own `same`/`opposite`/`either` and
the OSRM/Mapbox `approaches` words `curb`/`unrestricted`, which are
aliases for `same` and `either`. Both spell the same request, on this
surface and on the HTTP API.

oneOf.description:
The side the location itself projects to — the kerb, resolved
against the locale's driving side (the left kerb in the UK, the
right in Germany).
The far side of the road from the location.
No side preference.
Alias for `same`, from the OSRM/Mapbox `approaches` vocabulary.
Alias for `either`, from the OSRM/Mapbox `approaches` vocabulary.

RouteLocation.description:
One location of a `route` request: a coordinate, plus the optional
kerbside approach for arriving at it.

A bare `{lat, lon}` is still a complete location — every kerbside field
is optional and omitting all of them is exactly the request that was
made before they existed.

preferred_side.description:
Which side of the street to arrive on (or depart from). `same` (or
`curb`) puts the vehicle on the door's side of the road, resolved
against the locale's driving side. Two honest limits: this is a
**snapping preference**, not a manoeuvre guarantee — the engine
prefers an edge on that side, it does not promise the driver never
crosses — and it needs a coordinate genuinely offset from the road
centreline, because a point on the centreline has no side.

street_side_max_distance_m.description:
Metres: further than this from the road centreline, the side of
street is treated as `none` and `preferred_side` does nothing.
Engine default 1000 m. Together with `street_side_tolerance_m` this
is a WINDOW: a pair that leaves no window (tolerance at or above
max distance) is refused here rather than answered with a route on
which the kerbside preference was silently inert.

street_side_tolerance_m.description:
Metres: nearer than this to the road centreline, the side of street
is treated as `none` and `preferred_side` does nothing. Engine
default 5 m.

TruckSpec.description:
Truck profile for routing: physical dimensions plus the ADR
dangerous-goods declaration. Omitted dimensions default to the EU
maximum authorised dimensions of Council Directive 96/53/EC (4.0 m
height, 2.55 m width, 16.5 m length, 40 t gross weight).

gross_weight_t.description: Gross combination weight in metric tonnes.

hazmat.description:
Whether the vehicle carries dangerous goods (ADR). Defaults to
false.

tunnel_code.description:
ADR 8.6.4 tunnel restriction code of the load, e.g. "B", "C5000D",
"B/D", or "(—)"/"none" for explicitly unrestricted. Leave unset if
unknown: a hazmat load without a code is conservatively treated as
code B (allowed only through category-A tunnels).

avoid.description:
Road features to avoid as a PREFERENCE. Rendered as the costing's
willingness factor set to zero — a thumb on the scale, not a ban.
The engine's own reference is explicit that a value of zero is not
guaranteed to avoid the feature entirely, and it does not: asking
to avoid tolls across the Dartford Crossing returns the same tolled
route, because the untolled alternative is fifty kilometres
further. Use `exclude` when you mean a ban.

bicycle.description:
Bicycle options (bicycle type, road/surface/hill preferences).
Requires costing "bicycle".

emissions.description:
The vehicle's emission declaration, for UK clean-air / low-emission
zone assessment. Given, the response's `zones` block names every
zone the route enters and what THIS vehicle pays there, with the
publishing authority cited. Without it a zone can only be named,
never priced. Needs the MapMap gateway, which holds the curated
zone dataset; the full dataset is readable at `GET /v1/zones`.

exclude.description:
Road features to exclude outright, rendered as the costing's hard
exclusion flag. Two things follow from that and both matter: a hard
exclusion can return NO ROUTE rather than a detour (excluding
tunnels on a Rotherhithe crossing has no answer), and the flags
depend on the routing engine's `allow_hard_exclusions` setting,
which the engine does not expose and nothing here can read — so
this is never promised, only requested.

exclude_polygons.description:
Areas to avoid — scenario analysis ("close this bridge and
re-route"): an array of polygons, each an array of `[lon, lat]`
pairs forming one exterior ring (GeoJSON-style, longitude FIRST).
Roads intersecting any ring are excluded from the search. Applies
to the Valhalla engine; unsupported on the GraphHopper engine,
where it is ignored.

landmarks.description:
Name landmarks in the turn instructions (default false): each
manoeuvre that passes a recognisable place — a petrol station, a
supermarket, a household-name chain — gains a
`landmark_instruction` like "Turn right just after the Shell
garage" beside the engine's own street-name instruction, which is
never replaced. Nothing is named unless it is recognisable from the
road, within 40 m of the junction and not tagged as closed, so many
routes come back with none: a wrong landmark is worse than no
landmark. Needs the MapMap gateway, whose place index does the
lookup.

pedestrian.description:
Pedestrian options (lit-street preference, wheelchair/blind type,
hiking difficulty). Requires costing "pedestrian".

rationale.description:
Explain the route (default false): re-routes with each declared
truck constraint (truck costing) or avoidance-side routing
preference (auto, bicycle, pedestrian, motor_scooter) relaxed and
reports the ones that actually changed the route as
`rationale.avoided[]`. Opt-in — it costs up to 1 + N extra routing
calls, one per declared field plus one combined probe, and it is
billed for the ones it actually makes: at most 8 in total,
typically fewer, and 1 when there is nothing to probe. Against the
hosted gateway each probe is its own metered route call, which is
exactly what `POST /route` with `rationale: true` charges for its
own fan-out, so the two surfaces price the same explanation the
same way.

scenic.description:
Ask whether there is a prettier way (default false, `auto`
costing only). The route in `geometry_polyline6` is NEVER swapped:
what comes back is a peer offer beside it, in `scenic`, carrying
the plain sentence that justifies it. No sentence, no offer: a
route that scores well but cannot support one is dropped rather
than dressed up, and `scenic.reason` is then null, which is an
answer. Every candidate that lost says why in
`scenic.rejections[]` (`same_route`, `no_scenic_gain`,
`not_scenic_enough`, `over_time_budget`, `nothing_to_say`), so
"no prettier way" is always attributable. Opt-in because it
costs: at most two extra metered route computations, the same
billing shape as `rationale`. Needs the MapMap gateway, whose
basemap archive the scoring is measured against.

truck.description:
Truck profile (dimensions + ADR declaration). Requires costing
"truck"; when present, ADR dangerous-goods costing options are
merged into the request.

waypoints.description:
Optional intermediate stops, visited in order between origin and
destination.

name: route

AppliedAdr.description:
The ADR costing that was merged into a truck route request.

Every field here describes the **request**: the declared load and the
costing options built from it. Nothing here is an assertion about the
returned geometry — see [`TunnelEnforcement`].

costing_options.description: The exact Valhalla `costing_options` JSON merged into the request.

forbidden_tunnel_categories.description:
ADR tunnel categories **the vehicle** is forbidden from under the
worst-case reading of ADR 8.6.4 (conditional clauses assumed to
apply). Empty when unrestricted. This is not a claim that the
returned route contains no tunnel of these categories — read
[`AppliedAdr::tunnel_enforcement`] for what was actually applied.

hazmat.description: Whether the profile declared dangerous goods.

tunnel_code.description:
Canonical ADR tunnel restriction code applied ("B/D", "(—)", …),
or null when no code was declared.

tunnel_enforcement.description:
What the router did with `forbidden_tunnel_categories`, and the
boundary of the resulting guarantee.

AppliedAvoidance.description:
What the avoidance lists actually did, reported back so a 200 is never
readable as a certificate.

avoid.description: The `avoid` values that were applied, echoed back.

caveats.description:
The caveats that apply to this request, in words fit to repeat to a
user. Always present when anything was applied.

costing_option_fields.description:
The engine costing-option fields these words became, e.g.
`{"use_tolls": 0.0, "exclude_ferries": true}`. This is the whole of
what was sent — there is no hidden second mechanism.

exclude.description: The `exclude` values that were applied, echoed back.

AvoidedConstraint.description:
One constraint or preference the route provably changed for, derived
by route divergence (see [`RouteRationale`]).

baseline.description:
What the probe compared against: "relaxed_to_non_binding" (truck
constraints set to explicitly non-binding values),
"engine_default" (preference removed so the engine default
applies) or "cap_lifted" (a hard cap raised to its maximum).

basis.description:
Always "route_divergence": the entry was derived by re-routing
without the field and diffing geometry, not from sign or
map-feature data.

constraint.description:
The costing-options field that was relaxed ("height", "use_hills",
…, or "combined").

diverged_length_m.description: Length of the diverging span along the constrained route, metres.

fields.description: For kind "combined": the constraint fields that only bind together.

kind.description:
Reason kind. Truck: "max_height", "max_width", "max_length",
"max_weight", "hazmat", "adr_tunnel". Preferences: "hill_avoided",
"surface_avoided", "road_avoided", "highway_avoided",
"toll_avoided", "ferry_avoided", "living_street_avoided",
"primary_road_avoided", "unlit_street_avoided",
"hiking_difficulty_limited", "access_profile". Any costing:
"combined". There is deliberately no "incident_avoided" or
"traffic_delay_avoided": the engine consumes no live incident or
traffic-speed input, so no divergence can be attributed to them.

location.description: Where the constrained and unconstrained routes part ways.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation, honest about the method.

time_saved_s.description:
Travel time the constraint costs (unconstrained is this much
faster), seconds. Zero when the alternative is no faster.

value.description:
The declared value for the field (null for "combined"). NOTE: for
truck this is the vehicle's dimension, not the infrastructure
limit — the physical restriction is not identified.

note.description:
Why the count is what it is, when there is something to say: the
per-route lookup cap was reached, or the deployment has no place
index at all. Absent means the number is simply the number, so a
zero with no note means this route genuinely passes nothing
recognisable rather than that landmarks could not be looked up.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

ManeuverOut.description: One turn-by-turn instruction of a computed route.

country.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the road the manoeuvre starts on, e.g.
`"GB"`. This and the road fields below come from the MapMap gateway's
road walk: present when the route was computed through the gateway
(GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY) and the map knows the road, absent
otherwise. Never inferred.

distance_m.description: Length of the maneuver in metres.

driving_side.description:
The side of the road traffic keeps to there, `"left"` or `"right"`;
present only when the road's country is known.

duration_s.description: Estimated duration of the maneuver in seconds.

instruction.description: Written instruction, e.g. "Turn right onto Main Street".

landmark_instruction.description:
The same manoeuvre anchored to a recognisable place, e.g. "Turn
right just after the Shell garage" — present only when the request
set `landmarks: true` and a place near the junction cleared the
salience bar. Prefer reading this aloud when it is there: it is how
a passenger would give the direction. `instruction` is always the
engine's own and is never replaced.

ref.description:
Route numbers of that road (`"; "` separated, e.g. `"A27"` or
`"I 5; US 101"`); absent when it carries none, never read from a
street name.

road_class.description:
Engine road class of that road (`motorway`, `trunk`, `primary`,
`secondary`, `tertiary`, `unclassified`, `residential`,
`service_other`).

speed_limit_posted.description:
The posted limit as the sign shows it, in the road's own unit:
`{"type":"known","value":30,"unit":"mph"}` (plus `"national":true`
for a national limit), `{"type":"unlimited"}` or `{"type":"unknown"}`.
Read from the road the manoeuvre mostly travels along.

speed_limit_sign.description:
The speed-limit sign family there: `"vienna"` (roundel) or
`"mutcd"` (US and Canadian rectangle).

speed_limit_unit.description:
The unit speed limits are posted in on that road, `"mph"` or
`"km/h"`, from its country (never from the request's units).

subdivision.description:
ISO 3166-2 subdivision of that road where the map carries one, e.g.
`"GB-ENG"` or `"US-CA"`.

RouteRationale.description:
Why the route goes the way it does — the `route` tool's opt-in
rationale block, computed for truck, auto, bicycle, pedestrian and
motor_scooter costings. **Method honesty:** the routing engine exposes
no exclusion set, so entries are derived by re-routing with each
declared constraint or preference relaxed
(`basis: "route_divergence"`); this proves a field was binding and
where, but never names the physical restriction or feature (the
specific signed bridge, hill or unlit street). No live traffic or
incident data enters the comparison and no delay is ever estimated
from one — the engine has no live speed field.

avoided.description:
The declared constraints or preferences that changed the route,
with locations and costs. Empty when nothing was binding.

caveats.description: The method's limits, spelled out for relaying to users.

note.description: Why the list is empty or incomplete, when it is.

ScenicOffer.description:
The scenic assessment beside a route: a peer offer, never a
substitution.

The fields here are the ones a client must actually read before
saying anything. `block` keeps the gateway's whole answer beside them
so a figure can always be audited back to the source that produced
it, rather than to this mapping.

alternative_geometry_polyline6.description:
The scenic route's own geometry, polyline6, when there is one to
offer. `geometry_polyline6` on the route itself is byte-for-byte
what the same request returns without the flag.

available.description:
Whether scenery could be assessed at all on this deployment. When
false, `note` says why and nothing below was measured: that is
"we could not look", never "there is nothing there".

block.description:
The gateway's whole `scenic` block, verbatim: candidates, feature
shares, tile coverage, metering and budget.

caveats.description: The standing limits of the method, for relaying to users.

chosen.description:
Which route the assessment would offer: `"fastest"` (the quick way
is already the pretty one, or nothing beat it) or `"scenic"`.

extra_time_s.description:
How much longer the offered route takes than the fastest one,
seconds, and the sentence for it. Absent when nothing was offered.

note.description: Why no assessment ran (only when `available` is false).

reason.description:
The plain, speakable sentence behind the offer. **Null is an
answer**: nothing on this corridor measured above the floor, so
no claim is made rather than one being invented.

rejections.description:
Why each candidate that lost lost. Empty when none did. Relay it:
it is what makes "no prettier way" an attributable answer instead
of a shrug.

spoken.description:
The trade phrased for speech, e.g. "About seven minutes longer
than the quick way." Prefer reading this aloud over the seconds.

ScenicRejection.description: Why one candidate route was not offered.

detail.description:
The code in words, including the minutes an `over_time_budget`
candidate would have cost, so raising the budget is an informed
choice rather than a guess.

source.description:
Where the candidate came from: `"fastest"`, `"engine_alternate"`
or `"no_motorway"`.

TunnelEnforcement.description:
How the declared ADR tunnel code reaches the routing engine, and what a
returned route therefore does — and does not — prove.

This block exists because [`AppliedAdr::forbidden_tunnel_categories`] is
a statement about the **load** (ADR 8.6.4 applied to the declared code),
and on its own it reads like a statement about the **route**. It is not
one. The engine excludes a road only where the routing graph records an
ADR tunnel category for it, and that category is derived from OSM
`hazmat:*` tagging. Coverage is therefore uneven: a corridor with no
such tagging is not excluded and looks, in the response, exactly like a
corridor that was checked and cleared.

The field is emitted on every `applied_adr`, so a caller can never
receive the categories without the boundary that qualifies them.

basis.description:
How the code is applied. `"graph_adr_tunnel_category"`: merged into
`costing_options.truck.adr_tunnel_code` and matched, during the
search, against each road's ADR tunnel category as recorded in the
routing graph.

caveat.description: What an unchanged route does and does not prove, in one sentence.

route_certified.description:
Whether the returned route has been checked against a tunnel
inventory *after* it was computed. Always `false`: exclusion happens
during the search, and only for roads the graph has a category for.
A 200 is not a compliance certificate, and must not be relied on as
one.

applied_adr.description:
The ADR costing merged into the request, or null when no truck
profile was given.

avoidance.description:
What `avoid`/`exclude` became, and the caveats that go with it
(only when either list carried something).

duration_s.description: Total estimated travel time in seconds.

geometry_polyline6.description:
Full route geometry as a Google encoded polyline with six digits of
decimal precision (polyline6).

landmarks.description:
The landmark-annotation summary (only when `landmarks: true` was
requested): how many manoeuvres gained a `landmark_instruction`,
and a `note` when the per-route cap was hit or the deployment has
no place index. A zero with no note means this route genuinely
passes nothing recognisable.

maneuvers.description: Ordered turn-by-turn maneuvers across all legs.

rationale.description:
Why the route goes this way (only when `rationale: true` was
requested; computed for truck, auto, bicycle, pedestrian and
motor_scooter costings).

scenic.description:
The scenic peer offer (only when `scenic: true` was requested):
whether there is a prettier way, the sentence that justifies it,
what the detour costs, and why every candidate that lost lost.
The route above is never swapped for it.

summary.description: One-line human-readable summary of the route.

zones.description:
Clean-air / low-emission zones this route enters and what the
declared vehicle pays in each, with the publishing authority cited
(only when `emissions` was declared). Passed through verbatim from
the gateway's curated dataset — the same figures `GET /v1/zones`
publishes, so a charge can always be audited back to its source.
